title: Enhancing Work Zone Capacity by a Cooperative Late Merge System Using Decentralized and Centralized Control Strategies
application_family: Cooperative merging / coordinated gap creation / ramp coordination
supporting_metric: work-zone capacity = maximum observed throughput (traditional 1,526; decentralized CV 1,781 (+17%); centralized CAV 2,209 veh/h (+45%)), delay, queue length, lane-change duration, open/closed lane speed and headway differences
evidence_setting: microsimulation (VISSIM with external C++ lane-change DLL), I-64 Kentucky two-to-one work-zone lane closure, 25% trucks, CV share 20-100% with 60% compliance (decentralized) and 100% CAV (centralized), 30 seeds x 28 scenarios

Capacity is estimated as the maximum throughput of each system.
